error_direction_rationale: Every output is exact integer-cents arithmetic over the caller's values, so the only approximation direction is the Additional Medicare threshold reduction: the statute reduces the threshold by section 3121(b)(2) wages, while this node's single wage input is OASDI wages, so Medicare-only wages above the OASDI base understate the Additional Medicare Tax. That direction is conservative toward no finding and is mitigated by the named WAGE_INPUT_ABOVE_BASE_DIVERGENCE flag (reachable, fixture v14). No other output can understate.

derived_from.clause_path: SSA contribution and benefit base table, 2025 and 2026 rows, with self-employment rates
Instructions for Schedule SE (Form 1040) (2026): floors, church employee income, combined businesses
Instructions for Form 8959 (2025): threshold chart, SE income at Schedule SE line 6, wage reduction, line 13
Pub 334 (2025) ch.1 rate split and wage-base rule; ch.10 regular method times 92.35 percent

branches.branch: A tax of 12.4 percent on self-employment income.
A tax of 2.9 percent on self-employment income, with no maximum [SSA table; Pub 334 ch.1].

A 0.9 percent tax on self-employment income above 250000 dollars on a joint return, one half of that amount for a married taxpayer filing separately, and 200000 dollars in any other case, for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2012.
The applicable threshold is reduced, but not below zero, by wages taken into account under section 3121(b)(2).
The instructions reduce the threshold by TOTAL Medicare wages, while the caller input carries OASDI wages only, so Medicare-only wages above the OASDI base escape the reduction.
Net earnings from self-employment are gross income less the attributable deduction equal to net earnings times one half of the sum of the 1401(a) and 1401(b)(1) rates, i.e. 92.35 percent of profit.
The 12.4 percent tax applies only to net earnings up to the excess of the year contribution and benefit base over the wages taken into account under section 3121(b)(2).
No tax arises on net earnings below 400 dollars; the floor is applied to non-church net earnings separately.

branches.clause: 26 USC 1402(j)(2)(B) with Schedule SE (2026) 108.28 dollar floor
branches.branch: Church employee income below 108.28 dollars is excluded (the 100 dollar substituted net-earnings floor over 92.35 percent reproduces the income floor).
The 100 dollar net-earnings floor applies to church income separately; church net earnings below 100 dollars contribute nothing even when the income passes the 108.28 filing floor.
The 1402(a)(12) deduction applies to church employee income notwithstanding 1402(j)(1), so church income scales by 92.35 percent like all other earnings.
The deduction is one half of the 1401 taxes OTHER THAN the 1401(b)(2) tax, so the Additional Medicare Tax is excluded from the deduction base.

branches.clause: SSA contribution and benefit base table
branches.branch: The base is year-specific (176100 for 2025, 184500 for 2026); it is never extrapolated to an unpinned year.

branches.clause: SSA base table plus Schedule SE (2026) What's New
branches.branch: Any tax_year absent from the pinned year table computes nothing, because no base or optional-method constant may be extrapolated to it.

branches.clause: Schedule SE (2026) Fiscal Year Filers; Pub 334 ch.10
branches.branch: A fiscal-year filer must use the rate and base in effect when the fiscal year begins; this node is calendar-year keyed and a caller who cannot express a calendar year is refused rather than approximated.

branches.clause: 26 USC 1402(a) optional-method sentences and 1402(l); Schedule SE (2026) Part II; Pub 334 ch.10
branches.branch: The farm and nonfarm optional methods are out of this version's compute path; a request for them refuses by name instead of falling through to the regular method.

branches.clause: Form 8959 (2025) instructions; Schedule SE (2026) combined businesses
branches.branch: A self-employment loss is not considered for this tax; the caller supplies the combined figure across businesses, so a negative combined profit floors at zero and is flagged.

branches.clause: Values-only input contract (estate rule; spec section 1.3)
branches.branch: Every input is a value; a present null, a wrong type, a non-finite number or an out-of-domain string refuses with a named code and never coerces, and a hostile preimage never throws out of buildArtifact.

branches.clause: Schedule SE (2026) More Than One Business; Pub 334 ch.10
branches.branch: A loss in one business offsets another inside the combined figure the caller supplies; the node does not take per-business inputs.

assumption_of_use.value: net_se_profit as the single combined figure across businesses
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's own Schedule C / Schedule F totals and the instructions' combine rule
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller supplying the combined profit

branches.clause: Schedule SE (2026) Community Income, Qualified Joint Ventures, Joint Returns, Partnership Income or Loss
branches.branch: Allocation rules (community income, separate Schedules SE per spouse, K-1 box 14 code A) are documentation-only; the node takes one person's combined values.

assumption_of_use.value: the caller's already-allocated personal combined values
assumption_of_use.source: the caller's allocation under those rules

branches.branch: RRTA compensation is compared to the threshold separately and never reduces the SE threshold; the node models neither the RRTA-side computation nor any input for it, which is correct for the SE threshold and leaves the RRTA side unmodelled.
The section 162(l) premium deduction affects income tax, not SE tax, and its only SE-adjacent interaction runs through the optional methods, which are out of this version; no input exists for it.
